%1$d accesses · %2$d denied · %3$d more counted per interval
%1$d more accesses come from interval counts and are not included above. Intervals count every access, while the system may merge individual records, so the two are counted apart.

Individual records: camera, microphone, location and a few others have individual records, which the system keeps for 7 days. Their time precision and merging are up to the system, so the number of records need not equal the number of accesses.

Interval counts: other permissions only have counts per interval, which the timeline lists separately with their bounds. Intervals count every access, while the system may merge individual records, so the two are counted apart. When an interval partly overlaps individual records, it counts only the accesses beyond them. Because records may be merged, that number can be slightly high.

Denials: the system only counts denied attempts per interval, adding one for every refusal. That differs from how individual records count accesses, so the two numbers cannot be compared directly. Denials are included in the summary and the per-app statistics, not in the timeline. No recorded denial does not prove there were no attempts.

Range: an interval belongs to the range its end falls in, and one that crosses the start of the range keeps its full count. Up to 30 days can be shown, also measured by interval end. Older intervals carry unreliable times and are left out. With history persistence on, every saved individual record can be shown, and periods that were not saved are filled from intervals within 30 days.
The chart always covers the last 7 days of accesses. Retention and precision depend on the device.
Why save: the system keeps individual records for the last 7 days only. Older accesses remain only as counts per interval, without their times.

What is saved: the individual records of the permissions ticked on this page, whatever the history page shows. They are saved once when turned on. After that, the permissions the history page shows are saved as it refreshes, and the rest when the app is opened, at most every 6 hours. Only camera, microphone and location have individual records, so only those are listed.

Gaps: periods that were not saved, for example when AppOpsNext was not opened for 7 days, are filled from the system\'s interval counts. Periods older than 30 days have no reliable data to fill them and stay empty.
Storage: records stay on this device, are never uploaded and are excluded from backups. Up to 100,000 are kept, oldest removed first.
When off: nothing more is saved. Saved records are kept but not shown, and can be deleted on this page.

Unreadable records: this happens when the file is damaged or was written by a newer version of AppOpsNext, for example after a downgrade. The file is left as it is. A version that can read it continues from there, or deleting everything starts over.

Counts show how many times an access was reported. A permission that reports constantly, such as location during navigation, can be given a reporting interval in the monitor settings. Only apps in this user profile are monitored.
Enter between one second and %1$d minutes.
When each of these settings is useful. This page only explains and changes nothing. Which of your apps fits each case is up to you.
A location app you open and use yourself
While it is open you already know it is using location. What you want to hear about is the rest of the time.\n\nSuggested: off screen only · a minute or more · silent
An app you suspect of checking location quietly

You want to be told each time, as a pop-up rather than a count that climbs while you are not looking. A one-minute interval turns a burst of checks into a single alert.\n\nSuggested: off screen only · every minute · pop up
The camera or microphone turning itself on
This should not be happening often, so nothing gets folded together and every one interrupts.\n\nSuggested: off screen only · no limit · pop up
Checking that a permission you just denied is really blocked
Only the refusals answer that question. The accesses that went through are in the way.\n\nSuggested: refused only · no limit · pop up
These are read one at a time and each read means something, so none should be missed. A read while you are using the app matters too.\n\nSuggested: no limit · leave off-screen-only off
Watching a permission for the first time
Some report far more often than you would expect. Start with an interval, watch it for a few days, and take it off once you know it is quiet.\n\nSuggested: every 30 seconds · silent

Noise: many of these permissions are used constantly by ordinary apps. Watching one without giving it an interval can fill the notification within seconds.\n\nCompatibility: only the usual shortlist has been tested.
